# Intraday Capital Recycling — Feasibility Evaluation

*Generated by `scripts/eval_intraday_capital.py` · Yahoo 1-hour bars **2024-10-14 → 2026-09-22** (479 sessions, 23 traded vehicles incl. SATA and index ETFs) · book = published walk-forward replay (`walkforward_gated_replay`) · costs per side: 2 bp deep ETFs, 6 bp thin ETFs & SATA.*

## Question

Can capital be lent out **intraday** — and returned by the close so the daily book is untouched — to boost return on top of the Overall strategy without adding meaningful risk? Two proposed sources:

1. **Idle cash / SATA** — sell the SATA park after the open, trade, buy SATA back by the close.
2. **Calm open positions** — sell a held sleeve whose price looks quiet today, trade the proceeds, buy the sleeve back by the close at roughly the same price.

A third source is benchmarked because it dominates both when the account allows it: **(3) intraday margin** — buying power used and closed out before the close. IBKR charges margin interest on *overnight* debit balances, so a flat-by-close trade needs nothing pulled from the book.

## The identity that decides it

Selling held sleeve *A* at 10:30 to buy *B*, then reversing at the close, is exactly the book **plus an intraday long-B / short-A swap**:

```
increment = r_B(10:30→close) − r_A(10:30→close) − costs(A round trip) − costs(B round trip)
```

So source (2) only pays if **(a)** there is a *B* with a positive net edge, **(b)** *A*'s intraday drift is ≤ 0 on the days you pick, and **(c)** the extra variance of `r_B − r_A` is worth it. Source (1) needs only (a) plus covering the SATA round trip; source (3) needs only (a). Parts A–D test each piece.

## Part A — how much capital the sources actually free

| Profile | Mean idle SATA weight | Days SATA > 5% | Days SATA > 20% | Mean held weight on predicted-calm days | Sessions with any calm holding |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Balanced | 0.5% | 1% | 1% | 6.9% | 33% |
| Growth | 0.2% | 1% | 1% | 7.0% | 33% |
| Aggressive | 0.0% | 0% | 0% | 7.5% | 33% |

The gate water-fills the funded sleeves to their caps, so **the book is almost always fully deployed** — the SATA park is a rounding error in the replay (the live IBKR record is similar: cash under ~5% of NAV on most execution days, with the occasional larger residual while an exit waits for a new entry). Source (1) has very little capital to lend.

## Part B — does a “calm” position come back to the same price?

Sale at the 10:30 bar close, buy-back at the session close; *calm* is predicted from as-of data only (bottom tercile of the ticker's trailing 20-day intraday |move| **and** a first hour < 80% of its 20-day norm).

| Sessions | n | Mean 10:30→close (bp) | Median \|miss\| (bp) | \|miss\| > 0.5% | \|miss\| > 1% |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Held, every session | 4444 | +11.7 | 71 | 62% | 38% |
| Held, predicted calm (as-of) | 334 | +15.0 | 60 | 58% | 35% |
| Not held (for reference) | 4178 | -10.7 | 105 | 72% | 52% |

* **Held sleeves drift up intraday**: +11.7 bp per session from 10:30 to the close (t = 3.6); overall a held sleeve earns +32.0 bp overnight and +10.4 bp open→close. Lending out a position on an average day gives that drift away — the trend engines are long *because* the drift is positive.
* **Calm is only mildly predictable from as-of data**: median |miss| 60 bp on predicted-calm days vs 72 bp otherwise, and calm held sleeves still drift up (+15.0 bp) — so the swap still gives away the drift on the very days it is meant to be free.
* **“About the same price” does not hold**: even on predicted-calm days the buy-back misses the sale by >0.5% 58% of the time and by >1% 35% of the time. Around the drift that miss is a coin flip — added variance as large as any edge the freed capital could earn.

## Part C — is there an intraday trade worth funding?

Every rule on every vehicle, one unit per signal; *net* is per trade after costs. **H1 / H2** split the sample at 2025-10-09 — a real edge must be positive in both halves.

| Rule | Entry | n | Gross (bp) | Net (bp) | t (net) | Hit | Net H1 | Net H2 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Naive intraday long (open→close) | open | 10740 | -1.3 | -9.0 | -2.9 | 48% | -6.6 | -11.4 |
| Intraday momentum: sign(1st hr) → last 30m | 15:30 | 10712 | -0.6 | -8.3 | -11.3 | 39% | -9.0 | -7.6 |
| LETF rebalance flow: sign(day so far) → last 30m | 15:30 | 10715 | -2.2 | -9.9 | -13.5 | 38% | -12.2 | -7.5 |
|   … only when \|move\| > 1σ | 15:30 | 3250 | -2.9 | -10.6 | -7.2 | 40% | -11.4 | -9.9 |
| 1st-hr continuation: sign(1st hr) → 10:30..close | 10:30 | 10712 | +2.9 | -4.8 | -2.0 | 48% | -3.2 | -6.4 |
|   … long-only | 10:30 | 5716 | +3.8 | -4.0 | -1.2 | 49% | +1.4 | -9.5 |
| 1st-hr reversal when \|move\| > 1σ | 10:30 | 2325 | -6.6 | -14.3 | -2.8 | 45% | -20.3 | -8.9 |
| 1st-hr dip buy (move < −1σ) → close | 10:30 | 992 | -10.6 | -18.4 | -2.4 | 49% | -41.5 | +1.6 |
| Gap fade when \|gap\| > 1σ (open→close) | open | 1444 | +3.0 | -4.5 | -0.4 | 47% | +2.6 | -10.4 |
| Gap-down buy (gap < −1σ, open→close) | open | 651 | -9.8 | -17.5 | -1.1 | 48% | -34.7 | -3.7 |
| Add to HELD sleeves open→close (trend on) | open | 4444 | +10.4 | +2.1 | +0.5 | 49% | +5.3 | -1.4 |
| Buy NOT-held sleeves open→close | open | 4178 | -15.8 | -23.5 | -3.8 | 47% | -23.3 | -23.7 |

* **No rule is net-positive in both halves.**
* The rule a researcher would have picked after year one (**Add to HELD sleeves open→close (trend on)**, +5.3 bp net in H1) earned **-1.4 bp** net in H2 — the textbook out-of-sample fade.
* The last-30-minute rules (intraday momentum; the leveraged-ETF rebalance flow) are **negative even gross** here: the effect documented on SPY in older samples is not present in this universe/period, and a 30-minute hold cannot carry a round-trip cost anyway.
* The only rules near zero are *long exposure to sleeves the engines already hold* — i.e. more of the same trend bet, levered intraday, not a separate source of return. The repo's own BTC hourly model is no help either: its out-of-sample direction accuracy is 50.15% (`BTC_README.md`).

## Part D — portfolio overlays (Balanced, intraday-data window)

Each overlay adds its intraday P&L to the replay's daily return on the 507 weekdays of the window. Rules are the three least-bad from Part C (selected in-sample, so this is an *optimistic* bound). Each day's signals share the capital equally, so a rule's per-*day* mean can sit below its per-*trade* mean when its winners cluster on days with many signals; and because the overlay trades the same names the book holds, its variance stacks on the book's and costs compounding (volatility drag).

| Variant | Total | CAGR | ΔCAGR | MaxDD | Sharpe | ΔSharpe |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline — published replay (Balanced) | +384.7% | +125.7% | +0.0pt | -22.7% | 2.74 | +0.00 |
| (1) idle SATA → 1st-hr continuation, long-only | +386.2% | +126.1% | +0.4pt | -22.7% | 2.74 | +0.00 |
| (2) calm-position swap → 1st-hr continuation, long-only | +328.3% | +111.8% | -14.0pt | -22.6% | 2.53 | -0.20 |
| (3) intraday margin 25% NAV → 1st-hr continuation, long-only | +334.8% | +113.5% | -12.3pt | -26.1% | 2.38 | -0.36 |
| (3) intraday margin 50% NAV → 1st-hr continuation, long-only | +287.3% | +101.1% | -24.7pt | -29.7% | 2.03 | -0.70 |
| (1) idle SATA → Add to HELD sleeves open→close (trend on) | +386.1% | +126.1% | +0.3pt | -22.7% | 2.74 | +0.00 |
| (3) intraday margin 25% NAV → Add to HELD sleeves open→close (trend on) | +358.5% | +119.4% | -6.4pt | -28.6% | 2.36 | -0.38 |
| (3) intraday margin 50% NAV → Add to HELD sleeves open→close (trend on) | +329.9% | +112.2% | -13.5pt | -34.6% | 2.03 | -0.70 |
| (1) idle SATA → Naive intraday long (open→close) | +377.9% | +124.1% | -1.6pt | -22.7% | 2.71 | -0.03 |
| (3) intraday margin 25% NAV → Naive intraday long (open→close) | +322.4% | +110.3% | -15.5pt | -27.4% | 2.25 | -0.49 |
| (3) intraday margin 50% NAV → Naive intraday long (open→close) | +264.1% | +94.8% | -31.0pt | -32.4% | 1.83 | -0.91 |

The (1) rows barely move in either direction because they act on ~0.5% of NAV — noise, not an edge. Every overlay with real capital behind it (2, 3) lowers CAGR *and* Sharpe.

For scale: adding **+5 CAGR points** needs ≈ **1.9 bp per session on the whole NAV** — e.g. a trade earning 8 bp net every day on 25% of NAV. Nothing in Part C comes close.

## Verdict

* **Source (1) — idle cash / SATA: not worth building.** There is almost no idle capital (Part A), SATA already earns ~13%/yr on it, and the SATA round trip (~12 bp) costs more than the best intraday edge found (+2.1 bp net per trade).
* **Source (2) — lending out calm positions: rejected.** It is strictly worse than (3): the same B-leg risk *plus* a short-A leg that (i) gives up the held sleeves' positive intraday drift, (ii) adds a buy-back miss of ~60 bp median even on predicted-calm days, (iii) pays two extra spreads, and in a taxable account (iv) realises gains on every sale (short-term) or triggers wash-sale deferral on losses.
* **Source (3) — intraday margin: the only sound funding route, but there is nothing profitable to fund.** Across 12 standard rules × 23 vehicles no intraday trade has a net edge that survives an in-/out-of-sample split. Levering the book's own longs intraday is the least-bad use, and it adds risk roughly in proportion to return — not the free boost being sought.
* **Recommendation: do not add an intraday layer.** The strategy's edge is a multi-day trend premium, largely earned overnight; the intraday session is where it is thinnest. If intraday work is revisited it should start from a *demonstrated* intraday signal (tested on this harness first), funded by intraday margin — never by selling core positions.

## Caveats

* Yahoo 1-hour bars (~2 years, the maximum available); entries/exits at bar closes, no queue position or partial fills. Costs are tiered assumptions — the *Gross* column shows the rules fail before costs too, so the verdict does not hinge on them.
* 1-hour granularity cannot test sub-hour signals (opening-range breakouts, VWAP reversion). Those need tick/1-minute data and would face the same cost and funding arithmetic.
* The replay's weights are Balanced; Growth/Aggressive hold even less SATA.
* Pattern-day-trader rules apply to margin accounts under $25k equity; the paper account (~$96k) is above that. Margin availability, not idle cash, is the binding constraint for source (3).
* Regenerate with `python scripts/eval_intraday_capital.py` (numbers move with the data window).
